method: Real documents, not PubChem grids: the pixel-exact method of build_ground_truth.py does not apply. Every structure was located by reading the PDF itself - pdftotext -layout and pdfimages where a text layer exists, pdftoppm page renders at 45-400 dpi where it does not. Each resolved molecule required TWO independent views to agree: a PubChem record reached from something PRINTED IN THE DOCUMENT (an INN, a full IUPAC name, a Chinese chemical name, or - where the document prints no name - a SMILES structure search on the drawn reading) AND a reading of the drawing itself. NEW IN THIS ROUND: where the document prints a systematic IUPAC name, that name was parsed with OPSIN (py2opsin 1.2.0) to a SMILES and the resulting InChIKey used to fetch the CID via PUG-REST /compound/inchikey/. That route is deterministic and, unlike PUG-REST /compound/name/, cannot silently substitute a tautomer or drop a stereodescriptor - see the nintedanib group, where /compound/name/nintedanib returns the 2-hydroxyindole tautomer rather than nintedanib. Every SMILES was round-tripped through RDKit Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.MolFromSmiles(s)) and its InChIKey recomputed with RDKit and checked against PubChem's. Per-molecule `confidence` is one of: name_match (a name printed in the document resolves to the CID and the drawing agrees), drawing_read (the document prints NO name; the structure was read off the drawing and confirmed against a PubChem record by structure or InChIKey search), generic, or unresolved. `pixel_verified` is false everywhere - it is not achievable on real documents.
excluded: Structures that are DRAWN but carry no resolvable SMILES are held in each group's `unscoreable` array, NOT in `molecules`. That split is load-bearing: score_run.py calls Chem.MolFromSmiles(m['smiles']) on every entry of `molecules` and a null raises TypeError before its own error message. `unscoreable` holds Markush/R-group generics (generic: true), counter-ion generics, structures with no second independent view (confidence: unresolved), and BOOKKEEPING rows that describe a SET of depictions rather than a compound so that the arithmetic between `structures_drawn` and the row counts is legible. Repeat drawings of one compound are collapsed to ONE row, because score_run.py matches predictions to molecules by NAME and counts recall per row.
page_extracts: Eleven of the twenty-five files are PAGE EXTRACTS, flagged per group by `is_page_extract` with the kept range in `pages_kept`. In those groups every page number - in molecules[].page, in unscoreable[].page and in the prose of the group note - refers to the ORIGINAL PUBLISHED DOCUMENT, not to the extract, and `structures_drawn` counts the original. The other fourteen files are the complete document as published.

page_numbering: Page values are PDF page INDICES of the ORIGINAL publication, 1 = the first page of the file (and for the eleven page extracts they are still the original's indices, not the extract's). Two caveats. (a) On WIPO A1 documents the printed footer number is usually ONE LESS than the PDF index because the cover sheet is unnumbered, and a few entries in the WIPO groups quote the printed footer number instead - treat any page value in a WO group as +/-1. (b) On US patents the printed COLUMN numbers run two per PDF page, so a reference such as 'p12 col1' means the PDF page, not the printed column. Page values are informational; score_run.py matches predictions to molecules by NAME and never reads them.
